subject: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server

messages.author: e5ff05958bd1f6bd
messages.subject: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
parts:
I'm writing a shiny app to be run from a linux server. As part of the app I aim to record and playback audio to the user using the audio library:

observeEvent(input$record, {
             # record audio
x <- rep(NA_real_, 44100*2*3) # for 3 seconds
     # start recording into x
wait(record(x, 44100, 2)) 
     
# record audio
save.wave(x, paste( input$name,".wav",sep=""))
                       }

# PLAYBACK SOUND
observeEvent(input$play, {
wait(play( v$x ))
})

When running this on my own machine there is no problem, however when running the app from the linux server I get the following:

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:34971
Warning: Error in record: no audio drivers are available
Stack trace (innermost first):
    67: record
    66: wait
    65: observeEventHandler [/srv/shiny-server/ethnoling/app.R#156]
     1: runApp

I was under the impression the server would use the user's audio driver to send and receive audio data to the server. Is that not how it works? Do I need an audio driver on the server too? Sorry, I do statistics in R, I'm not a developer :)

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Recording User Audio from Shiny R Server
parts:
No, this isn't going to work--it'll attempt to record *from the server*, meaning, using whatever audio device is on the server. So you'll just get a recording of fan noise or whatever. :-\

In order to record and playback audio from the user, you'll need to use the browser's recording/playback capabilities, which can be done but requires someone to write the JavaScript (both to record/playback the audio and to send it to the Shiny server). This is probably at least a day or two of work for a good JS + Shiny developer, but the result would be reusable by everyone.
